# Error correction, inference, and topological order {#sec-error-correction}

A symmetry charge can remain exactly fixed while its location becomes impossible to infer. The preceding chapters described this as strong-to-weak order. Error correction asks a closely related question: after local errors have occurred, can an observer infer enough about them to recover a global quantum state? The useful connection is between **recovering information** and **distinguishing physically different error classes**. It is more precise than the loose statement that noise destroys order.

We will construct the connection from stabilizers, derive its statistical mechanics, and identify exactly where a quantum-memory interpretation enters. Throughout this chapter syndrome measurements are perfect unless stated otherwise, the noise is an unconditioned channel, and logarithms are natural. A decoder may use the complete syndrome record. Its classical computational cost is a separate issue from whether recovery is possible in principle.

## Stabilizers as constraints {#sec-code-stabilizers}

A Pauli string is a tensor product of single-qubit operators chosen from $I,X,Y,Z$, with an overall phase. Two Hermitian Pauli strings either commute or anticommute. Let $S_1,\ldots,S_r$ be independent, commuting Hermitian Pauli strings on $n$ qubits, with no product equal to $-I$. Their common $+1$ eigenspace is a stabilizer code. Its projector is

$$
P_{\mathcal C}=\prod_{a=1}^r\frac{I+S_a}{2}.
$$ {#eq-code-projector}

Each independent constraint halves the dimension, so $\dim\mathcal C=2^{n-r}=2^k$. The code encodes $k$ logical qubits. The maximally mixed code state is $\rho_{\mathcal C}=P_{\mathcal C}/2^k$. Expansion of the product gives an especially useful form,

$$
\rho_{\mathcal C}=2^{-n}\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}S,
\qquad S(\rho_{\mathcal C})=k\ln2,
$$ {#eq-code-stabilizer-density}

where $\mathcal S$ is the group generated by the stabilizers. The trace of a nonidentity Pauli string vanishes; this checks normalization directly.

A Pauli error $E$ changes the measured value of $S_a$ precisely when it anticommutes with it. Write the syndrome as bits $s_a$:

$$
S_aE=(-1)^{s_a}ES_a.
$$

Errors $E$ and $ES$ with $S\in\mathcal S$ act identically on every codeword. Errors with the same syndrome can nevertheless act differently: their ratio may be a logical operator that preserves the code space but changes its encoded state. Correcting the syndrome alone does not determine whether a logical error remains.

For a stochastic Pauli channel $\mathcal N(\rho)=\sum_EP(E)E\rho E^\dagger$, the decoder should infer an equivalence class, not the exact microscopic history. Fix a reference error for each syndrome, and label the remaining logical Pauli action by $\ell$. Then

$$
P(s,\ell)=\sum_{E\in(s,\ell)}P(E),\qquad
P(\ell|s)=\frac{P(s,\ell)}{\sum_{\ell'}P(s,\ell')}.
$$ {#eq-code-posterior}

The optimal syndrome-dependent Pauli correction picks the most probable $\ell$. Its success probability is

$$
P_{\mathrm{succ}}^{\mathrm{ML}}=\sum_s\max_\ell P(s,\ell).
$$ {#eq-code-ml}

“Maximum likelihood” here sums every history in a class. A minimum-weight decoder chooses a single low-weight representative; entropy can make that choice suboptimal.

### Why correcting a subspace is possible

The exact recovery theorem originates in the general theory of quantum error-correcting codes [@knill1997].

There is an exact criterion behind the syndrome construction. Let $V$ encode a logical Hilbert space into the physical one, so $V^\dagger V=I_L$. A collection of errors $E_a$ is exactly correctable on that entire space when

$$
V^\dagger E_a^\dagger E_bV=c_{ab}I_L.
$$ {#eq-code-kl}

This is the Knill-Laflamme condition. It says that overlaps between error images carry no information about which logical vector was encoded. To see why that matters, use a dilation $|\psi_L\rangle\mapsto\sum_a E_aV|\psi_L\rangle\otimes|a\rangle_E$, with the error weights absorbed into $E_a$. The environment matrix has elements $\langle\psi_L|V^\dagger E_b^\dagger E_aV|\psi_L\rangle$. If it depends on the logical input, the environment has learned information about a superposition and the system alone cannot reverse the interaction on every input. Independence for every vector forces the matrix to be scalar, by the polarization identity. Correcting arbitrary entangled inputs requires this full operator condition, rather than agreement only on a chosen basis.

The sufficiency is constructive. Diagonalize the positive matrix $c$ by mixing the error operators. In that error basis, $V^\dagger F_a^\dagger F_bV=d_a\delta_{ab}I_L$. For $d_a>0$, each $F_aV/\sqrt{d_a}$ is an isometry, and different $a$ have orthogonal image spaces. A recovery can identify that image space without learning the logical vector, then invert its isometry. An error label can thus be measured harmlessly when it contains no logical information. This is exactly what an ideal syndrome does.

For Pauli stabilizer codes, distinct syndromes give orthogonal spaces. Errors differing by a stabilizer act identically on the logical input. Errors with the same syndrome but different logical actions violate the scalar condition when included together. Decoding is therefore an inference problem about which of those conflicting alternatives occurred.

At any finite size, a stochastic channel assigning positive probability to every Pauli error generally cannot be corrected exactly: its rare logical errors remain possible. A threshold asserts **approximate** recovery with failure tending to zero as size grows. It does not assert the exact condition for the complete error set at every nonzero noise rate. This distinction explains why a positive-noise threshold and the existence of arbitrarily unlikely undetectable logical errors are compatible.

### Worked example: a three-qubit repetition code

Take $S_1=Z_1Z_2$, $S_2=Z_2Z_3$, with codewords $|000\rangle$ and $|111\rangle$. For independent bit flips of probability $p<1/2$, the trivial syndrome can arise from $I$ or $X_1X_2X_3$. Their probabilities are $(1-p)^3$ and $p^3$. A nontrivial syndrome likewise has a one-flip representative and its complementary two-flip representative. Choosing the lower-weight member gives

$$
P_{\mathrm{fail}}=3p^2(1-p)+p^3.
$$

The logical bit is more reliable than one physical bit for small $p$. This code does not protect an arbitrary qubit against arbitrary noise: a single $Z_i$ already acts as a logical phase error. The example illustrates both the value and the limitation of inference from a restricted noise model.

## Toric-code geometry before statistical mechanics {#sec-toric-code-geometry}

Put a qubit on every edge of a square lattice with periodic boundaries. Define

$$
A_v=\prod_{e\ni v}X_e,\qquad
B_f=\prod_{e\in\partial f}Z_e,\qquad
H_{\mathrm{TC}}=-\sum_v A_v-\sum_f B_f.
$$ {#eq-toric-hamiltonian}

A star and a face share zero or two edges and therefore commute. On a torus, $\prod_vA_v=\prod_fB_f=I$. Euler's formula $V-E+F=0$ then gives $k=E-(V-1)-(F-1)=2$: four ground states.

A string of $Z$ operators along an open direct-lattice path anticommutes with $A_v$ at its two endpoints. The endpoint violations are called electric anyons, or $e$ particles. An $X$ string on the dual lattice creates magnetic $m$ particles at its endpoints, where $B_f=-1$. Contractible closed strings are stabilizers. Noncontractible strings wind around a handle and act on logical qubits.

The crucial distinction is topological. A syndrome specifies the endpoints of an error chain. It does not specify whether that chain wound around the torus. Local stabilizer measurements cannot see this difference, because a noncontractible closed string has no endpoints. This is why local constraints can protect nonlocal information. The foundational error-correction interpretation was developed in @dennis2002 and extended to faulty syndrome measurements in @wang2003memory.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-decoding-process
%%| fig-cap: "Decoding infers a logical class by summing compatible microscopic histories."
%%| fig-width: 3
%%| out-width: "45%"
flowchart TB
  A[Local Pauli errors] --> B[Endpoints: measured syndrome]
  B --> C[Many compatible chains]
  C --> D[Sum probabilities within each homology class]
  D --> E[Infer winding class]
  E --> F[Recover logical state]
```

For the moment consider only $Z$ errors. Represent an error by binary edge variables $e_a\in\{0,1\}$, with probability

$$
P(e)=p^{|e|}(1-p)^{N_e-|e|}.
$$

The syndrome is the boundary $s=\partial e$, computed modulo two. Adding the boundary of a face changes the error by $B_f$ and leaves its effect on the code unchanged. On a torus, two chains with the same endpoints differ by face boundaries and one of four homology classes $h\in\mathbb Z_2^2$.

## Deriving the Nishimori condition {#sec-code-nishimori}

Choose one representative $e$ consistent with a measured syndrome. Introduce signs $\tau_a=(-1)^{e_a}$. Multiplying by a face stabilizer can be represented by an Ising variable $\sigma_f=\pm1$ on each face: an edge between faces $f$ and $f'$ is toggled when $\sigma_f\sigma_{f'}=-1$. A fixed sign pattern $\eta_a(h)$ inserts the required noncontractible twist. Thus every chain in class $h$ has signs

$$
(-1)^{e'_a}=\tau_a\eta_a(h)\sigma_f\sigma_{f'}.
$$

For one binary error variable,

$$
p^{e'_a}(1-p)^{1-e'_a}
=\frac{e^{K(-1)^{e'_a}}}{2\cosh K},
\qquad e^{-2K}=\frac{p}{1-p}.
$$ {#eq-code-nishimori}

This identity fixes the effective inverse temperature $K$. It is not an independently adjustable laboratory temperature. Summing the probabilities in an error class therefore gives, up to an $h$-independent redundancy factor,

$$
Z_h(\tau)=\sum_{\{\sigma_f\}}
\exp\left[K\sum_a\tau_a\eta_a(h)\sigma_f\sigma_{f'}\right],
\qquad
P(h|s)=\frac{Z_h(\tau)}{\sum_{h'}Z_{h'}(\tau)}.
$$ {#eq-code-partition}

This is a random-bond Ising model. For disorder averages, we may use the actually drawn physical error as the reference chain: then $\tau_a=-1$ independently with probability $p$, tied to $K$ by @eq-code-nishimori. This matched disorder-temperature relation is the Nishimori condition. It is a device for computing ensemble-averaged performance, not a prescription requiring the decoder to know the error. A representative chosen from the syndrome alone need not have independent bond signs; changing that representative changes variables and relabels the four sectors without changing the inference problem.

To see why a transition is relevant, compare free energies of twisted and untwisted sectors,

$$
\Delta F_h=-\ln\frac{Z_h}{Z_0}.
$$

In a phase with a macroscopic domain-wall cost, incorrect winding sectors are suppressed as the system grows. Their posterior probabilities vanish, and recovery becomes asymptotically reliable. When a spanning domain wall costs only order one, distinct windings can have comparable posterior probabilities. Global logical information is no longer recoverable with probability approaching one.

The familiar threshold near $p\simeq0.109$ belongs to the square-lattice toric code with independent errors of one Pauli type, perfect syndrome information, and optimal decoding. It should not be transplanted to depolarizing noise, correlated channels, different lattices, finite measurement rounds, or a particular practical decoder. The spin-model mapping explains the meaning of the threshold; the numerical value is a property of that model, obtained by solving its disordered statistical mechanics. Information-theoretic mixed-state diagnostics reproduce this threshold in the specified toric-code setting [@fan2024diagnostics].

### The origin of quenched rather than annealed averages

In an experiment, a syndrome is drawn once and then used for inference. The relevant calculation first normalizes the posterior for that syndrome and only afterward averages the outcome over syndromes. An expression such as $\mathbb E_\tau[\ln Z_\tau]$ is consequently natural. Replacing it by $\ln\mathbb E_\tau[Z_\tau]$ changes the inference problem. Replica calculations sometimes make this distinction easy to overlook: the replica number required for an entropy or fidelity limit need not be the integer replica number describing a purity.

## Quantum memory requires a reference {#sec-code-coherent-info}

Recovering one known state is a weak test. A channel that discards the input and prepares that state passes it. To test a code as a quantum memory, entangle its logical space $L$ with an inaccessible reference $R$:

$$
|\Phi\rangle_{RL}=2^{-k/2}\sum_{a=1}^{2^k}|a\rangle_R|a\rangle_L,
$$

encode $L$ into the physical qubits $B$, and apply the noise only to $B$. Define coherent information by

$$
I_c(R\rangle B)=S(B)-S(RB)=-S(R|B).
$$

For a noiseless code, $RB$ is pure and $I_c=k\ln2$. For the stochastic Pauli channel above, distinct pairs $(s,\ell)$ produce orthogonal syndrome-resolved logical Bell states. Hence $S(RB)=H(s,\ell)$. Tracing out $R$ makes the logical state maximally mixed in every syndrome sector, so

$$
S(B)=H(s)+k\ln2,
\qquad
I_c=k\ln2-H(\ell|s).
$$ {#eq-code-coherent-posterior}

This derivation uses a maximally entangled logical input, Pauli noise, and orthogonal perfect syndromes. It is not a general formula for arbitrary non-Pauli channels. It nevertheless exposes the physics particularly clearly: inaccessible logical uncertainty subtracts directly from coherent information.

At vanishing posterior logical entropy, correction returns every logical state and its entanglement with $R$. At extensive uncertainty among logical Paulis, it cannot. For the toric code, $k=2$ is fixed, so “extensive” here means uncertainty over the full logical algebra rather than a quantity proportional to physical volume. Coherent information is a useful diagnostic for this family, not automatically the capacity of a general channel after arbitrary block coding or multiple uses.

### Worked example: quantum information can become classical

Consider one encoded qubit with an effective logical dephasing channel

$$
\mathcal D_q(\rho_L)=(1-q)\rho_L+q\overline Z\rho_L\overline Z.
$$

Applied to half a Bell pair, it creates a mixture of two orthogonal Bell states, giving $I_c=\ln2-h(q)$, where $h(q)=-q\ln q-(1-q)\ln(1-q)$. At $q=1/2$, $I_c=0$. Yet $|0_L\rangle$ and $|1_L\rangle$ remain perfectly distinguishable. The memory retains a classical bit and loses the phase needed for an arbitrary qubit. This is the simplest reason that “topological memory survives” must specify whether classical or quantum information is meant.

For independent $X$ and $Z$ noise, the syndrome/Pauli-class bookkeeping includes both types of logical uncertainty. When only one type proliferates, a classical logical algebra can remain. When both complementary logical observables are randomized, even that remnant can disappear. Correlations between $X$ and $Z$ errors require their joint posterior; treating them as independent would discard useful information.

The distinction between one codeword and its logical family also enters phase classification. For the toric code under local noise, correlation-preserving renormalization and truncated decoding channels establish a low-noise mixed topological phase; within that framework, destroying logical information requires leaving the toric-code phase [@sang2024rg]. This is a model-specific connection between recoverability and phase structure, with locality and approximation hypotheses on the channels.

## From charge inference to gauging {#sec-code-gauging}

Why do global symmetry problems and topological decoding problems repeatedly produce the same spin models? A useful bridge is gauging. In a spin system, a global $\mathbb Z_2$ operation flips every spin simultaneously. Gauging introduces link variables and makes a local flip into a redundancy, with a Gauss constraint at each vertex. In a pure gauge description, a fixed-point toric-code wavefunction can be constructed explicitly:

$$
|\psi_{\mathrm{TC}}\rangle\propto
\prod_v(I+A_v)|0\cdots0\rangle_Z.
$$ {#eq-code-gauge-wavefunction}

The starting state has $B_f=+1$ everywhere. Applying all products of stars preserves those flux constraints and sums over gauge-related configurations. A global redundancy $\prod_vA_v=I$ accounts for one repeated term. Additional noncontractible choices produce the four torus sectors.

The state is a **coherent** sum. Replacing it by a classical probability distribution over the same configurations removes off-diagonal matrix elements between configurations. The resulting loop ensemble can retain global winding constraints and classical sector labels without preserving all quantum logical superpositions. Gauging thus turns questions about delocalized charge and domain walls into questions about flux, strings, and logical sectors. It does not assert that every ungauged SW-SSB phase is equivalent to every mixed topological phase.

The correspondence is especially transparent for Abelian noise models, where errors and charges form additive groups. A non-Abelian theory requires fusion channels as well as charge labels; @sec-generalized-symmetry develops that extra structure.

## What doubling does and does not establish {#sec-code-errorfield}

Vectorizing a density matrix turns a channel into an operator on ket and bra copies. In a topological theory, those copies carry conjugate topological data. A noise event can create correlated excitations across them. This motivates interpreting decoherence as a defect coupling the two copies, and a noise-driven transition as condensation at that defect. The errorfield-double construction develops this idea for Abelian topological order [@bao2026errorfield].

For the argument's physical content, imagine an error string on the ket copy together with its partner on the bra copy. Their endpoint pairs can proliferate under averaging. Operators that braid nontrivially with those proliferated pairs no longer distinguish coherent sectors in the same way. The surviving algebra depends on which paired excitations proliferate, which is why different error channels can leave different logical information.

A vectorized state $|\rho\rangle\rangle/\sqrt{\tr\rho^2}$ weights eigenstates by their probabilities rather than their square roots. Its entanglement and ordinary correlators describe purity-normalized quantities. An integer-replica transition in this doubled state can therefore differ from a fidelity or optimal-recovery transition. To connect a doubled calculation to a physical memory, identify the channel, input/reference, retained record, replica limit, and recovery criterion explicitly.

Measurements provide another instructive comparison. A measurement-prepared state with its outcomes retained may be correctable by classical feedforward. Discarding the record produces a different density matrix. The relation between measurement-prepared order, classical statistical models, and decoding protocols was made explicit in @lee2022decoding. The distinction between conditioning and averaging is indispensable when comparing such constructions with decoherence.

## Limits of the correspondence {#sec-code-limits}

There are at least four independent axes. First, noise may be Pauli or coherent. Coherent amplitudes can interfere, so a positive classical probability model may no longer exist in the same form. Second, syndrome measurements may themselves fail; repeated extraction then produces a spacetime inference problem. Third, a practical decoder can fail below the information-theoretic threshold because its algorithm ignores correlations. Fourth, a mixed-state phase definition can preserve more data than a particular decoder tests.

Strong-to-weak order concerns nonlinear distinguishability of charge-modified states. Error correction concerns distinguishability and reversibility of an entire family of encoded states. The overlap is powerful because both ask what global information remains after local noise, but neither phrase replaces the other's hypotheses. A density matrix with nonzero topological negativity need not encode a recoverable qubit, and a classical loop ensemble can contain global conditional information without ordinary bipartite entanglement.

## Exercises and worked solutions {#sec-code-exercises}

### Exercise 1: entropy of a stabilizer marginal

Let $\rho=2^{-n}\sum_{S\in\mathcal S}S$, and let $A$ contain $n_A$ qubits. Suppose the subgroup $\mathcal S_A$ supported entirely inside $A$ has $r_A$ independent generators. Find $S(A)$.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Partial trace annihilates every Pauli string acting nontrivially outside $A$. Thus $\rho_A=2^{-n_A}\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_A}S_A$. This is the normalized projector onto the common $+1$ eigenspace of $r_A$ constraints, of rank $2^{n_A-r_A}$. Its nonzero eigenvalues are all $2^{-(n_A-r_A)}$, and $S(A)=(n_A-r_A)\ln2$. The formula applies to this flat stabilizer density matrix; a general weighted mixture of stabilizer sectors need not have a flat spectrum.
:::

### Exercise 2: posterior probability, not representative weight

A measured syndrome has two logical classes. Class 0 contains one history of probability $0.10$ and class 1 contains four histories of probability $0.04$ each. Which class should a maximum-likelihood decoder select? What is its conditional success probability?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
The total syndrome probability is $0.10+4(0.04)=0.26$. The class posteriors are $5/13$ and $8/13$. Select class 1, with success probability $8/13$. Picking the most probable individual history selects class 0 and succeeds only with probability $5/13$. The example isolates the configurational entropy that becomes a partition sum in @eq-code-partition.
:::

### Exercise 3: logical dephasing with a classical flag

For the one-qubit channel $\mathcal D_q$, suppose the environment supplies the error bit $a\in\{0,1\}$ to the decoder. Calculate coherent information when that classical flag is included in the output.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
The joint state is $\sum_a p_a|a\rangle\langle a|_C\otimes|\Phi_a\rangle\langle\Phi_a|_{RB}$. Its entropy is $H(a)=h(q)$. The $BC$ marginal has entropy $\ln2+h(q)$ because each conditional $B$ state is maximally mixed. Therefore $I_c(R\rangle BC)=\ln2$ for all $q$. Applying $\overline Z^a$ recovers the Bell state exactly. The same physical interaction is reversible or irreversible depending on whether its record is available.
:::

### Exercise 4: a twist costs information

Suppose one syndrome has two possible logical classes with partition functions $Z_0$ and $Z_1=e^{-\Delta}Z_0$, with $\Delta\geq0$. Compute its maximum-likelihood success probability and its contribution to the conditional logical entropy.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
The posterior is $P_0=1/(1+e^{-\Delta})$, $P_1=1/(1+e^{\Delta})$. Success is $P_0$. Its entropy is $h(P_1)$. If $\Delta=cL$ with $c>0$, $P_1\sim e^{-cL}$ and $h(P_1)\sim(cL+1)e^{-cL}$, so this syndrome becomes reliably correctable. If $\Delta$ stays finite, its uncertainty remains nonzero. A threshold statement requires averaging over the syndrome distribution and controlling rare syndromes as well as typical ones.
:::

### Exercise 5: torus versus sphere

Count toric-code logical qubits on a sphere using $V-E+F=2$.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
There are again two redundant stabilizer constraints. Thus $k=E-V-F+2=0$. The ground state is unique on a sphere. Local anyon excitations and their braiding still exist, but there are no noncontractible cycles carrying ground-space logical qubits. Topological order is more than ground-state degeneracy on one chosen manifold.
:::
